Thank you for thinking of me. I am afraid I cannot take that on before April.
Ah. Is it the workload, or is it the timing?
The timing. Monday afternoons are a clash with something I cannot move, and I would rather not double-book myself and let you down halfway through.
That is fair. Could you do it if we pushed the whole thing back a month?
In April, yes, and gladly. Would it be possible to keep the same slot but on Thursdays?
Probably. I will look at the rota. And for the record, you did that well. Most people give me four reasons and then say yes anyway.
I have been that person. It ends with me stretched thin and everybody slightly disappointed.

I said yes to everything for about four years, and I want to be precise about why, because it was not generosity. It was fear. I thought that if I turned anything down, the next thing would not be offered to me, and at twenty-two that felt like a real risk. What actually happened was that I became the person you asked when you needed something done badly, because I was too stretched to do anything properly. Nobody says that out loud, but everybody notices it. The thing that changed it was a sentence somebody gave me, and I have used it a hundred times since. I am afraid I cannot take that on this month, but I could do it in April. It is one sentence and it does three things. It says no clearly, so nobody is left guessing. It gives no excuse, which sounds harsh and is actually kinder, because an excuse invites a negotiation. And it offers something real, which is what stops it from being a door closing. If there is one skill I would give a first-year student, it is that. Not the confidence. The sentence.

Hi, this is a message for everybody on the Tuesday rota, so apologies if this does not apply to you. We have a clash next week and I need to sort it out before Friday. The department has moved the seminar to Tuesday at ten, which is exactly when the lab session runs, and there is no version of next week in which both of those happen. So here are the two options and I would like an answer, not a preference. Option one, we push the lab session back to Thursday afternoon, same room, same length. Option two, we keep Tuesday and I record the seminar, which works but is honestly worse, because half the value of that seminar is asking questions in the room. If Thursday afternoon does not work for you, tell me now rather than on Wednesday. I would much rather reschedule something once, properly, than find out on the day that four people cannot come. Email is fine, one line is fine, and I am afraid I do need it before Friday.
